text:
sre-alex:heads-up: seeing a cluster of 504/timeouts from hosted inference customers starting ~08:12 UTC. Symptoms point to request queue saturation and continuous-batching backlog. customer report: repeated 504, then long tail p95->p99 spike. details below.

sre-alex:example curl + response body we got from customer:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXXX' -d '{"model":"open-XXX","input":"hello"}'
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
x-request-queue-depth: 128
x-continuous-batcher-queue: 2300
{"error":"upstream_timeout: request queue depth exceeded"}
```

sre-alex:metrics snapshot: ingress.request_queue_depth{region=us-east-1}=120, continuous_batcher.backlog=2300, served_tokens/s down 40%. spike started at 08:11 UTC and correlates with a tenant traffic burst (t-12345).

support-oncall:@sre-alex which regions/customers are impacted? any correlation with recent deploys?

sre-alex:mostly us-east-1 and eu-west-1. tenants t-12345 and t-54321 reported. no model deploy around 08:10 in hosted control plane, but infra shows a routing policy change at 08:20 (see bot).

deploy-bot:deploy: routing-policy-adjust-2026 by infra at 08:20 UTC — changelist: add overflow routing for dedicated-pool-b when hosted pool depth > 1000.

maria:@sre-alex I can dig into continuous-batcher settings. can you drop a link to the grafana panel or the tenant request_id/sample trace?

sre-alex:trace id for one slow request: trace-0a1b2c3d, attached span timeline: span[ingress -> router -> batcher.wait(1.2s) -> batcher.exec(0.9s) -> backend-call(1.5s) -> response]. notice long queue wait before exec. link: https://grafana.redwood/influx/d/queue/ingress?t=4491234567 (internal)

sanjeev:likely continuous-batcher backlog (kv cache spinup + cold model shards) + unbounded tenant burst. mitigation options: 1) enable early-reject on queue depth for hosted pool, 2) temporarily route overflow to warm standby pool, 3) reduce max_batch_size for high-latency models. I'll try 2 and 1 now.

sre-alex:@sanjeev please coordinate with support for customer comms. I'll enable additional alerting for queue_depth > 800.

sanjeev:started policy flip: overflow -> standby-pool (safe drain). also toggled early_reject=true for hosted pool watchers.

support-oncall:pinged customers t-12345/t-54321: noted mitigation and ETA ~10m. they reported fewer 504s after first flip.

maria:quick config diff I pushed for investigation:
```yaml
continuous_batcher:
  max_inflight_per_tenant: 64 -> 48
  max_queue_depth: 5000 -> 2500
  early_reject_threshold: 0.9 -> 0.7
```

maria:reduced inflight and tightened early_reject for hosted pools. want to run traffic replay for t-12345 to validate.

sre-alex:after toggles, p95 improved from 4.2s -> 1.1s, p99 still at ~3.8s for a small slice. tail still visible for requests that hit cold backend shards.

sanjeev:action items: create runbook entry "ingress-batcher-overflow" with steps: detect queue_depth > 2000, flip overflow routing, enable early_reject, scale standby pool, follow customer comms. also add alert: continuous_batcher.queue_depth > 2000 AND backlog_growth_rate > 100/min.

support-oncall:creating support tickets and adding mitigation notes. will update customers and close if stable. ticket refs: #SUP-7834 #SUP-7835.

maria:follow-up investigation: capture heap/profile of batcher workers to see if kv-cache warm-up amplifies backlog. will start capture and paste link.

sre-alex:thanks team. marking incident as mitigated for now. will file a short postmortem with timeline and recommended permanent fixes (model-aware batching heuristics + autosize standby pools). :thumbsup:
